Q128614.label: John Diefenbaker
Q128614.summary: John George Diefenbaker was the 13th prime minister of Canada, serving from 1957 to 1963. He was the only Progressive Conservative party leader between 1935 and 1979 to lead the party to an election victory, doing so three times, although only once with a majority of the seats in the House of Commons.

Q55910.label: Jerzy Buzek
Q55910.desc: Prime Minister of Poland (r. 1997–2001); President of the European Parliament (r. 2009–2012)
Q55910.summary: Jerzy Karol Buzek is a Polish politician who served as Prime Minister of Poland from 1997 to 2001. Since being elected to the European Parliament in 2004, he served as President of the European Parliament between 2009 and 2012. He is married to Ludgarda Buzek and is the father of Polish actress Agata Buzek.

Q3290214.label: Romanian parliamentary reform referendum
Q3290214.summary: A referendum on modifying the size and structure of the Parliament from the current bicameral one with 137 senators and 334 deputies to a unicameral one with a maximum of 300 seats was held in Romania on 22 November 2009, at the same time as the first round of the 2009 presidential election.

Q917606.label: Brioni Agreement
Q917606.desc: agreement which facilitated the cessation of hostilities between the JNA and Slovene forces in the Ten-Day War
Q917606.img: Slovenia Croatia and Yugoslavia location map.svg
Q917606.summary: The Brioni Agreement, also known as the Brioni Declaration is a document signed by representatives of Slovenia, Croatia, and Yugoslavia under the political sponsorship of the European Community (EC) on the Brijuni Islands on 7 July 1991. The agreement sought to create an environment in which further negotiations on the future of Yugoslavia could take place.

Q815718.label: 2009 Sumatra earthquakes
Q815718.summary: Two earthquakes occurred in late 2009 off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia. The first, on 30 September, had a moment magnitude of 7.6 at 17:16:10 local time. The epicenter was 45 kilometres (28 mi) west-northwest of Padang, West Sumatra, and 220 kilometres (140 mi) southwest of Pekanbaru, Riau.

Q2594918.label: Battle of Honkaniemi
Q2594918.summary: The Battle of Honkaniemi was fought between Finnish and Soviet forces on 26 February 1940. This battle was notable for being fought by tanks, the only time they were used en masse in combat by Finnish forces in the Winter War.

Q4872294.label: Battle of Shangshak
Q4872294.desc: battle of the 1944 Burma campaign during World War II
Q4872294.summary: The Battle of Shangshak took place in Manipur in the forested and mountainous frontier area between India and Burma, from 20 March to 26 March 1944. The Japanese drove a parachute brigade of the British Indian Army from its positions with heavy casualties, but suffered heavy casualties themselves. The delay imposed on the Japanese by the battle allowed British and Indian reinforcements to reach the vital position at Kohima before the Japanese.

Q3641958.label: Bombing of Pescara in World War II
Q3641958.wiki: Bombing of Pescara in World War II
Q3641958.summary: The bombing of Pescara was a series of attacks by the United States Army Air Force on the city of Pescara in Abruzzo, Italy during World War II. The raids caused thousands of civilian casualties and left 80 % of the city destroyed or damaged.

Q909414.label: Operation Mountain Fury
Q909414.summary: Operation Mountain Fury was a NATO-led operation begun on September 16, 2006 as a follow-up operation to Operation Medusa, to clear Taliban insurgents from the eastern provinces of Afghanistan. Another focus of the operation was to enable reconstruction projects such as schools, health-care facilities, and courthouses to take place in the targeted provinces.

Q131363430.label: 2024 Hama offensive
Q131363430.desc: HTS-led military operation during the Syrian civil war
Q131363430.img: Syrian rebels at Hama Military Airport.png
Q131363430.summary: The 2024 Hama offensive was a military operation launched by forces of the Syrian Salvation Government (SSG) and Turkish-backed rebel groups of the Syrian Interim Government (SIG) during the 2024 Syrian opposition offensive, a phase of the Syrian civil war. The operation, which was launched by the Military Operations Command, took place in the Hama Governorate.

Q3351142.summary: Sir Kariamanikkam Srinivasa Krishnan was an Indian physicist. He was a co-discoverer of Raman scattering, for which his mentor C. V. Raman was awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.

Q28774.label: reverse transcriptase
Q28774.desc: an enzyme which generates DNA from an RNA template, a process termed reverse transcription
Q28774.summary: A reverse transcriptase (RT) is an enzyme that uses an RNA molecule as a template to synthesize a complementary DNA molecule, through a process termed reverse transcription. Reverse transcriptases are used by viruses such as HIV and hepatitis B to replicate their genomes, by retrotransposon mobile genetic elements to proliferate within the host genome, and by eukaryotic cells to extend the telomeres at the ends of their linear chromosomes.

Q45670.label: Kingdom of Portugal
Q45670.summary: The Kingdom of Portugal was a monarchy in the western Iberian Peninsula and the predecessor of the modern Portuguese Republic. Existing to various extents between the mid-12th century and the early 20th century, it was also known as the Kingdom of Portugal and the Algarves after 1471, and was the main constituent of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, which existed between 1815 and 1822. It coexisted with the Portuguese Empire, the realm's overseas colonies.

Country: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
